nodes.description: SF-1 transcriptionally controls multiple steps of adrenal and gonadal development and steroidogenesis, regulating target genes including STAR, CYP17A1, CYP11A1, CYP19A1, AMH, LHB, and INHA. Reduced SF-1 dosage dysregulates this shared program, simultaneously impairing testis determination and differentiation, ovarian development and maintenance, and steroid-hormone biosynthesis. The same molecular lesion is therefore channeled into divergent, sex-dependent clinical outcomes.

Where the gonads are preserved in a 46,XY (SRXY3) patient, they should be brought into a palpable position by early orchidopexy and then kept under germ-cell-tumour surveillance, because dysgenetic gonads carry a raised risk of malignant germ cell tumour and of carcinoma-in-situ precursor lesions. Finding premalignant or malignant change is what prompts gonadectomy. The corollary is that reflex gonadectomy in infancy is not the default: because severely undervirilized SRXY3 infants may still virilize spontaneously at puberty, irreversible procedures should be deferred until sex assignment has been considered carefully.
